content.title: Find the Thing You Need
content.hook: A page can contain dozens or hundreds of elements. JavaScript needs a way to find the particular element it wants to work with.
content.context:
For this module, start with one reliable tool: `document.querySelector(...)`.

It accepts a CSS selector and returns the first matching element.
goals: Find specific elements in the page and recognize the difference between selecting the right element and changing it.

content.title: First example
content.text:
Given: ```html

Waiting

``` You can find it with: ```js const status = document.querySelector("#status"); ``` The `#` means "find the element whose id is `status`."

content.question:
What will `status` refer to after this line?

```js
const status = document.querySelector("#status");
```

options.text: The text `Waiting` as a plain string
The paragraph element in the page
A copy of the HTML file

feedback.correct: Correct answer: B. The paragraph element in the page
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: B. The paragraph element in the page

content.title: What if nothing matches?
content.text:
If the selector does not match an element, `querySelector` returns `null`.

That means your code has to be careful about assuming a match exists.

The useful debugging question is: **Did I select the element I think I selected?**

content.question:
A learner writes:

```js
const button = document.querySelector(".save");
```

But the page contains:

```html
<button id="save">Save</button>
```

What is the problem?

options.text: The selector asks for a class named `save`, but the element has an id named `save`.
The browser changed the id into a class.

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. The selector asks for a class named `save`, but the element has an id named `save`.
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. The selector asks for a class named `save`, but the element has an id named `save`.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** First find the exact element you mean. Then operate on it.
**Senior habit:** When a DOM operation fails, inspect the selection before blaming the operation.
